questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go somewhere where I could explore nature and have great nature experiences. It was also important that I was able to have courses in different subjects and themes. It was also important to me that the courses were taught in english, or another language that I already knew.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I got send most of the information on my Ku mail, furthermore there was a welcome meeting that I attended. Most of the information was quite easy to acces, but I had to find some information myself.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was an information meeting for new students which was quite informative as to where I could search for further information about almost amything.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Campus housing was available through a site called student housing. You could apply for different kinds of accommodation. All where some kind of dorm rooms, either with your own bathroom or without. I applied for a room with my own bathroom but with a shared kitchen, we were 9 people living together in one apartment, each with our own room and bathroom.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: We shared one big kitchen, the facilities were quite good. We have 2 stoves, ovens, microwaves etc. we shared 3 fridges and 1 freezer,

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It is a good way of getting to know other students from around the world, but be aware that not every apartment is very social, but it is still very nice to live with other people.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We had to find courses online and apply to them. The registration process in itself was not very difficult, but it was a bit of a hassle to find the courses available that semester, as it was not all updated in the course catalog.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was a help desk at the university,

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I first registered for courses that overlapped, so I had to reregister. Once that was done it was quite easy. It was not difficult to deregister from a course, the most difficult part was to find exactly which courses were available at which times, the course information pages were not the same, as the teacher was responsible for their own page.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Do not be afraid to reregister for another course if the first ones do not fit, just be sure to deregister from the exams.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was not as high as in Copenhagen. It was not easy, but the amount of reading was not as high. I only had mixed levels courses, so they were very general, and that might have something to do with the levels.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: On the other hand there was a lot of tests and assignments during the semester which is very different from my courses in Copenhagen,

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: I was enrolled in Anthropology of gender, environmental anthropology, Being Icelandic and Basic Icelandic 1.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Depending on your interest I found Being Icelandic and Basic Icelandic quite informative. I got to have a deeper understanding of the culture and learned a small bit of the language which I appreciated. I also enjoyed both the other courses, and they both awakened a deeper interest, but as they were mixed level open courses they were very general, so it should rather be seen as introductory courses, which I did not know when I registered for them.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I was on quite a lot of trips and spend a lot more money on renting cars than I had expected. I also ended up doing a ring road road trip which was quite expensive. Other than this I used a bit of money on furniture and decorations for my room as it was very sparingly furnished.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Coffee is quite inexpensive which was a really pleasant surprise. You can easily go to a cafe and only pay around 30-35 dkk for a coffee.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not join any clubs, as there were not many clubs and I did not find them very intriguing.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: In the beginning of the semester there were a few parties, I believe there might have been a soccer tournament and a beer pong tournament as well. All in all there was not that many activities available.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The welcome days,

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I would really recommend exploring as much of the country as possible. Especially in the beginning (or end) when the highlands are still open.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was quite similar to danish culture, but be aware that Icelanders are even more closed off that Danes in general.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Try to become friends with the Icelanders in your dorm, even though it can be a bit difficult,

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The closed off-ness.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The easy going way of living, even though it means that time management is not a great competence.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Utilize your free time to go on hiking and sight seeing trips, especially when the highlands are open.
 Don’t think to much about the money you are spending, it will be worth it.
Be open and try the local cuisine, even though it might not look appealing it is fun to try,

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you like hiking bring your gear with you as it is quite expensive to buy in iceland, if you do buy it there, be sure to get a tax free voucher, and get the money back in the airport,

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I loved all the nature, and I will definitely be coming back to Iceland sooner rather than later.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I expected to get a lot of local friends, which was quite difficult, as some are a bit stand off-ish to exchange students, but instead I got a lot of international (and danish) friends.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
